name: StripForge
description: Stripboard (Veroboard) layout in KiCad: strip copper, cuts and wire links in a normal .kicad_pcb, KiCad DRC and a printable build sheet.
description_full:
StripForge turns a KiCad project's real footprints and netlist into stripboard copper on B.Cu at a 2.54 mm pitch. It snaps THT parts to the hole grid, splits the strips by net with real copper gaps plus cut markers, places wire links (zero-ohm W jumpers that also go into the schematic), runs KiCad's DRC with schematic parity to catch shorts and opens, and writes a printable build sheet: the mirrored copper side with every cut, the component side, and checklists for cuts, slots, links, parts and a continuity check.

The PCB editor gets five toolbar actions: StripForge: Analyze, Build strips, Add links to schematic, Run DRC and Build sheet. Build strips saves the board, backs it up (<name>-pre-stripbuild.kicad_pcb, older backups rotate) and builds into it. You can move cut markers and links by hand; the next build keeps them.

KiCad 10 only, IPC plugin (enable the KiCad API in Preferences > Plugins). Beta: tested on one real board so far.
